title: Linux_XorDDoS_Botnet_Investigation_50c
description: Investigate and identify malicious activity in a network experiencing unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents. Your task is to investigate and identify any malicious activity related to the XorDDoS malware family, determine its scope, and recommend containment measures. This training will guide you through the process of analyzing systemd services, identifying persistence mechanisms, and examining network traffic patterns to detect and mitigate threats.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

To proceed to the next level, enter the word 'start' in the input field below.
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that communicates with an external host? The flag type is a service name.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, start by checking the systemd services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service`. Look for any unusual or recently created services. The service name is `bot-beacon.service`. This service is likely responsible for periodic external communication, which is a common behavior of malware.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd services are used to manage various processes in Linux. Malicious services often appear unusual or are recently created.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the systemctl command to list all services and look for any that seem out of place.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Network Traffic Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service that is generating the abnormal network traffic? The flag type is a service name.
levels.solution: To identify the service responsible for generating abnormal network traffic, investigate the systemd services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service`. Look for any services that might be responsible for network flooding. The service name is `bot-flood.service`. This service is likely generating excessive network traffic, which is a common characteristic of DDoS malware.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Network flooding services often generate excessive traffic, which can be detected by examining systemd services.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the systemctl command to list all services and look for any that might be responsible for network flooding.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The service name generating abnormal network traffic is `bot-flood.service`.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service? The flag type is a timer name.
levels.solution: To determine the persistence mechanism, examine the systemd timers using the command `systemctl list-timers`. Look for any timers associated with the suspicious service. The persistence mechanism is `system-update-checker.timer`. This timer ensures that the malicious service is automatically started after a system reboot, maintaining persistence.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Persistence mechanisms in Linux often involve systemd timers that ensure services start automatically after a reboot.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the systemctl command to list all timers and look for any associated with the suspicious service.
